result.topic_en: Euler expresses the ratio c/z of the Moon's mean to true distance as a cosine series, so that the apparent diameter and horizontal parallax of the Moon can be found directly; he gives the logarithms of the coefficients, the expanded series and its numerical values.
result.transcription:
De diametris apparentibus motuque horario vero solis ac lunae, in eclipsibus lunaribus. 385

Ad quodvis igitur tempus hinc tam diameter solis apparens cum ejus parallaxi horizontali, quam verus motus horarius assignari poterit.

§ 4. Diameter lunae apparens ejusque parallaxis horizontalis pendet ab ejus distantia a terra. Scilicet si distantia media ponatur $=c$, et distantia vera $=z$, erit, uti supra vidimus, diameter lunae apparens $=\frac{c}{z}\cdot 31'13\tfrac{1}{2}''$, *) et parallaxis lunae horizontalis $=\frac{c}{z}\cdot 56'39''$. Commodissime ergo primo quaeritur distantia lunae a terra $z$, ex qua cum sit $c=100000$, levi calculo tam diameter apparens quam parallaxis lunae horizontales definitur. Interim tamen quoque formula $\frac{c}{z}$ per divisionem evolvi poterit, sicque ex ea immediate tam diametrum apparentem, quam parallaxin horizontalem definire licebit. Ponamus loco coëfficientium numericorum litteras alphabeti, sitque
$\frac{z}{c}=1+k\cos v-\mathfrak{a}\cos V+\mathfrak{b}\cos(v+V)-\mathfrak{c}\cos(v-V)+\mathfrak{d}\cos\eta-\mathfrak{e}\cos 2\eta-\mathfrak{f}\cos(2\eta-2v)$
$-\mathfrak{g}\cos(2\eta+v)+\mathfrak{h}\cos(2\eta-v)+\mathfrak{j}\cos(2\eta+V)+\mathfrak{k}\cos(2\eta-V)-\mathfrak{l}\cos(2\eta-v+V)-\mathfrak{m}\cos(2\eta-v-V).$

§ 5. Coëfficientes ergo hi, quorum valores supra exhibuimus, sequenti modo per logarithmos determinabuntur, ut sit
$lk=8,7359900$   $l\mathfrak{d}=6,4639186$   $l\mathfrak{h}=8,0092614$
$l\mathfrak{a}=6,1580247$   $l\mathfrak{e}=7,8437310$   $l\mathfrak{j}=6,2771879$
$l\mathfrak{b}=6,2430230$   $l\mathfrak{f}=6,3091788$   $l\mathfrak{k}=6,3908075$
$l\mathfrak{c}=6,2803776$   $l\mathfrak{g}=6,5773131$   $l\mathfrak{l}=6,2581595$
$l\mathfrak{m}=6,0152034$

Quibus notatis habebimus convertendo fractionem $\frac{z}{c}$:
$\frac{c}{z}=1-k\cos v+\tfrac12 kk\cos 2v-\tfrac14 k^3\cos 3v+\mathfrak{a}\cos V-\mathfrak{b}\cos(v+V)+\mathfrak{c}\cos(v-V)$
[coefficient of $1$:] $+\tfrac12 kk$, $+\tfrac12\mathfrak{h}\mathfrak{h}$
[coefficient of $\cos v$:] $-\mathfrak{e}\mathfrak{h}$, $-\mathfrak{f}\mathfrak{h}$, $-\tfrac34 k^3$
[coefficient of $\cos V$:] $+k\mathfrak{b}$, $-k\mathfrak{c}$, $-\mathfrak{h}\mathfrak{l}$, $-\mathfrak{h}\mathfrak{m}$
[coefficient of $\cos(v+V)$:] $-\mathfrak{a}k$, $+\mathfrak{j}\mathfrak{h}$
[coefficient of $\cos(v-V)$:] $-\mathfrak{a}k$, $+\mathfrak{k}\mathfrak{h}$
$-\mathfrak{d}\cos\eta+\mathfrak{e}\cos 2\eta+\mathfrak{f}\cos(2\eta-2v)+\mathfrak{g}\cos(2\eta+v)-\mathfrak{h}\cos(2\eta-v)$
[coefficient of $\cos 2\eta$:] $-k\mathfrak{g}$, $+k\mathfrak{h}$
[coefficient of $\cos(2\eta-2v)$:] $+k\mathfrak{h}$
[coefficient of $\cos(2\eta+v)$:] $-k\mathfrak{e}$
[coefficient of $\cos(2\eta-v)$:] $-k\mathfrak{e}$, $-k\mathfrak{f}$
$-\mathfrak{j}\cos(2\eta+V)-\mathfrak{k}\cos(2\eta-V)+\mathfrak{l}\cos(2\eta-v+V)+\mathfrak{m}\cos(2\eta-v-V)$
[coefficient of $\cos(2\eta+V)$:] $-k\mathfrak{l}$, $+\mathfrak{b}\mathfrak{h}$
[coefficient of $\cos(2\eta-V)$:] $-k\mathfrak{m}$, $-\mathfrak{c}\mathfrak{h}$
[coefficient of $\cos(2\eta-v+V)$:] $+k\mathfrak{j}$, $-\mathfrak{a}\mathfrak{h}$
[coefficient of $\cos(2\eta-v-V)$:] $+k\mathfrak{k}$, $-\mathfrak{a}\mathfrak{h}$

§ 6. Restitutis ergo loco harum litterarum valoribus erit
$\frac{c}{z}=1,00160-0,05464\cos v+0,00148\cos 2v+0,00012\cos V$
$0,00069 \quad 8,73751 \quad 7,17095 \quad 6,07918$

*) Ad marginem: potius $31'14\tfrac12''$.

L. Euleri Op. posthuma T. II.   49

items.quote: Commodissime ergo primo quaeritur distantia lunae a terra $z$, ex qua cum sit $c=100000$, levi calculo tam diameter apparens quam parallaxis lunae horizontales definitur.
items.english: Most conveniently, therefore, one first seeks the Moon's distance z from the Earth; from it, since c = 100000, both the apparent diameter and the horizontal parallax of the Moon are found by an easy calculation.

items.quote: Interim tamen quoque formula $\frac{c}{z}$ per divisionem evolvi poterit, sicque ex ea immediate tam diametrum apparentem, quam parallaxin horizontalem definire licebit.
items.english: Meanwhile, however, the formula c/z can also be expanded by division, so that from it both the apparent diameter and the horizontal parallax can be determined directly.
